newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MOGILNY LEADS CANUCKS TO OT WIN OVER BLACKHAWKS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MOGILNY LEADS CANUCKS TO OT WIN OVER BLACKHAWKS.

text.p: Alexander Mogilny set up David Roberts' tying goal late in the third period, then scored the game-winner 84 seconds into overtime as the Vancouver Canucks rallied for a 4-3 win over the Chicago Blackhawks Thursday.

Mogilny came out of the penalty box after serving a boarding penalty and picked up a loose puck at the Blackhawks' blue line. He carried into the right corner and skated along the goal line before feeding Roberts, who poked the puck under goaltender Jeff Hackett.
"I knew he was going hard to the net so I just went hard to the net and he hit my stick and I was able to get it back to Hackett," Roberts said. "It was good timing and nice to get that third goal."

Vancouver intercepted a clearing attempt early in overtime and Mark Wotton had the puck at the top of the left faceoff circle. He slid a pass under the stick of a Chicago defender to Mogilny, who lifted a backhander that tipped off Hackett's pad and just inside the right goalpost.
Russ Courtnall had a pair of assists for the Canucks, who won for just the second time in their last 14 trips to Chicago.
The Canucks had been 1-13-1 when trailing after two periods this season.
In Hartford, Robert Kron lifted a rebound over Mark Fitzpatrick with 13.6 seconds left in overtime, giving the Whalers a 2-1 victory over the slumping Florida Panthers.
Hartford nearly won it at the end of regulation but Kron's deflection hit the left goalpost with 15.9 seconds left.
In Anaheim, Guy Hebert made 40 saves and Teemu Selanne and Paul Kariya each had a goal and an assist, leading the Mighty Ducks to a 3-1 victory over the New Jersey Devils.
Jari Kurri had the other goal for the Ducks, who have won four of their last five games.
Hebert turned aside the last 40 shots he faced and twice stopped Bill Guerin on breakaways.
In Buffalo, Jason Dawe scored twice and Dominik Hasek stopped 32 shots as the Sabres won their fourth straight game, 6-1 over the Montreal Canadiens.
Hasek (24-15-4) has stopped 75 of the last 77 shots he has faced and moved ahead of Colorado's Patrick Roy for the NHL lead with his 24th win.
The Sabres improved to 7-0-1 in their last eight home games and defeated the Canadiens for the fourth straight time.
In Detroit, John LeClair's goal with 9:30 left in regulation lifted the Philadelphia Flyers into a 2-2 tie with the Red Wings, who have only one win in their last nine games.
It was the 29th goal of the season for LeClair, who has scored in each of the last four games.
Trent Klatt had the other goal for Philadelphia, which snapped a six-game losing streak at Detroit. The Flyers are 1-0-3 in their last four games overall.
In Uniondale, New York, Derek King had two goals and an assist and five players added a goal and an assist apiece, powering the Islanders to an 8-1 rout of the Edmonton Oilers.

Bryan McCabe, Steve Webb, Derek Armstrong, Marty McInnis and Zigmund Palffy each had a goal and an assist for the Isles, who won for just the second time in their last 11 games (2-8-1). New York snapped a four-game home losing streak.
In Ottawa, Rob Tallas made 23 saves and Rick Tocchet and Kyle McLaren scored in a 52-second span of the third period as the Boston Bruins defeated the Senators 4-1.
Adam Oates and Brett Harkins also scored for the Bruins, who snapped a four-game losing streak.
The Senators could have tied Boston for fifth place in the Northeast Division with a win.

In San Jose, Owen Nolan had two goals and two assists and Jeff Friesen and Darren Turcotte also scored twice as the Sharks tallied four times in the second period en route to a 7-2 victory over the Los Angeles Kings.
Viktor Kozlov also scored and Ulf Dahlen and Andrei Nazarov each had two assists for the Sharks, who have won three of their last four games.

In Toronto, Wendel Clark returned from a 16-game absence forced by a broken thumb and had a goal and an assist and Doug Gilmour set up all five goals to help the Maple Leafs snap a season-high seven-game losing streak with a 5-3 victory over the Calgary Flames.
David Cooper, Rob Zettler and Mats Sundin also scored for the Leafs, who won for the first time in 1997 and improved to 5-1 in their last six home games against the Flames.
At Washington Brian Leetch scored his second goal of the game with 36.8 seconds remaining and the New York Rangers defeated the Capitals 5-3 after squandering a three-goal lead.

Adam Graves scored into an empty net with 21 seconds to go, sealing New York's second win in seven games. Sundstrom and Mark Messier each had three assists and Wayne Gretzky two for the Rangers, who beat Washington for the first time in four meetings this season.
